utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. A very good afternoon to everybody. May I ask the registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number case number IT-95-14/2-A, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I have the appearances for the parties. Prosecution first, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Helen Brady appearing on behalf of the Prosecution, and with me today Ms. Marie-Ursula Kind and our case manager Ms. Lourdes Galicia. And I'd like to extend apologies on behalf of Mr. Norman Farrell, our lead counsel, who can't be present today because he's ill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I wish him all the best. I know about this fact. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Mr. Naumovski, attorney-at-law from Zagreb, on behalf of Dr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the same as usual, Bozidar Kovacic for Mr. Mario Cerkez. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I take the opportunity at the same time to ask the two appellants whether they can follow the proceedings in a language they understand and is there any complaint about the conditions in the United Nations Detention Unit, or do you feel uncomfortable, or do you have reasons to believe to be ill?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT KORDIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Thank you for asking and thank you for giving me the opportunity to say what we think. I understand what you're saying. I don't have any objections to the Detention Unit conditions and I feel well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And please, Mr. Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT CERKEZ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for asking, Your Honour. I have no objections and my health condition is good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. This is in fact good news. You may be seated again. May I ask the parties, are there any pending matters, pending motions? Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. BRADY
utterances.text: Nothing from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From the side of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing on behalf of Mr. Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence team for Mr. Cerkez has no issues to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is an extraordinarily good situation, so I take it that there are no problems in relation to disclosure. But nevertheless, it's my duty to remind the Prosecution on what is now Rule 68, that notwithstanding the completion of an appeal, the Prosecutor shall disclose to the other party - here the parties - any material referred to in paragraph A, above that Rule 68(A), in the form as amended at 12 December 2003. Any other issues to be raised? And it's also an opportunity, no doubt, for the appellants themselves to raise any questions, if there should be any. I can see nobody who wants to take the floor. Then I can only express the hope that this will be the last Status Conference in this case. The Status Conference is hereby closed. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
